title: The Side-Channel Report
role: You are the maintainer of an ML-KEM implementation used by customers.
objective: Triage, fix and disclose a reported timing leak in decapsulation.
environment: A researcher reports that decapsulation takes measurably different time for valid and invalid ciphertexts, measured over the network from outside.

state_variables.key_safety: Protection of key material, starts at 60

stages.narrative: The report arrives with a measurement script.

choices.text: Acknowledge it, reproduce locally with statistical timing tests, and treat it as exploitable until disproved.
choices.feedback: Correct. Timing differences can be averaged out over many samples, so network jitter does not make a leak safe.

choices.text: Dismiss it: network jitter hides any difference.
choices.feedback: Attackers repeat measurements and use statistics; remote timing attacks have been demonstrated against real systems.
A fix that is not tied to a reproduced cause may leave the leak in place and gives you no regression test.

stages.narrative: You find that the check comparing the re-encrypted ciphertext with the received one exits at the first differing byte.

choices.text: Use a constant-time comparison and a constant-time (mask-based) selection of the output secret, or move to a maintained constant-time implementation, and add tests.
choices.feedback: Correct. Both the comparison and the choice between the real and the fallback secret must not depend on secret data in time or memory access.

choices.text: Add a random delay to the function.
choices.feedback: Random delay can be averaged away; the dependence on secret data remains.

choices.text: Allow the service only from the internal network.
choices.feedback: It reduces the number of attackers but not the flaw, and is not available to the customers who run your library.

choices.text: Run statistical timing tests in CI with many measurements, and check that compiler optimisations or CPU behaviour have not reintroduced a branch.
choices.feedback: Correct. Constant-time is a property of the compiled code on real hardware, so it needs measurement.

choices.text: Run unit tests that check only that decapsulation is correct.
choices.feedback: Correctness tests do not detect timing differences.
Reviewers and compilers both miss secret-dependent branches; measure.

stages.narrative: The fix is ready to ship.

choices.text: Publish a coordinated advisory with affected versions, the fix, mitigations and credit to the researcher, and advise key rotation where exposure is plausible.
choices.feedback: Correct. Users cannot protect themselves from a flaw they do not know about.

choices.text: Ship the fix quietly with no notice.
choices.feedback: Customers on older versions stay vulnerable without knowing, and the silence erodes trust when the issue becomes public.

choices.text: Hold the disclosure until after a marketing event.
choices.feedback: Delaying disclosure for convenience prolongs customers' exposure.

stages.narrative: The security team writes the post-mortem.

bands.title: Fixed and disclosed
bands.text: SUCCESS. The leak was reproduced, fixed in constant time, verified, and disclosed responsibly.

bands.title: Partly resolved
bands.text: PARTIAL. The immediate risk is reduced, but verification, disclosure or timing could have been stronger.

bands.title: Leak remains
bands.text: AT RISK. The flaw remains exploitable or customers lost trust in how it was handled.

resolution.concept_reveal: Timing side channels leak secrets through the duration of operations that depend on them. The cure is constant-time code (comparison and selection included), verified by statistical timing tests, plus responsible disclosure. Random delays and network restrictions are not fixes.

replayability_note: Different triage and disclosure choices change trust and exposure.
